title: 11th Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened with the minutes of three earlier sittings accepted and a committee seat change announced. Most of the part was question time for the Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, Mohamed Ameen: members asked about the delayed helicopter service, the huge number of vehicles and unregistered cars in Male', Island Aviation's losses, airport projects, and RTL ferry rollout in the atolls, and the minister said work was ongoing and some fixes needed law changes. The chair then opened nominations for a Judicial Service Commission seat (Husnee Mubarik was proposed and seconded), closed debate on the committee report recommending the Media and Broadcasting Commission president, and the Customs Service report from the Public Safety committee began to be presented, with a short recess. This part finishes the debate on the Security Services Committee's report on the Maldives Customs Service, which covers smuggled cigarettes and vapes, two lost 40-foot containers of cigarettes and lost import duty. Three members spoke, all supporting the report, with calls for people involved in the thefts to be investigated and held to account. Members then voted: Hussain Mubarik was approved 58-0 as the Majlis member on the Judicial Service Commission, the Media and Broadcasting Commission president nominee was approved 49-9, and the report's recommendations passed 58-0. The sitting closed with the next one set for Tuesday 28 October 2025 at 9:00. The text layer is garbled in places, so some details are not repeated.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ameen
positions: As Minister of Transport and Civil Aviation, said helicopter operations will be re-tendered after redesign and that a safety assessment found helicopters safe to operate.
Said Male' vehicle numbers grew because of weak past registration rules and that fixing the carrying-capacity limit is a city council duty needing law changes.
Said RTL ferry rollout is under way, Island Aviation costs are high and being cut, and airport and parking-building plans are in progress.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked why the promised helicopter service has not started and whether vehicle import controls or a cap are planned.
Asked what the ministry is doing to reduce deadly road accidents in Male'.
Asked what the government is doing to lower domestic air fares.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Asked whether helipads and helicopter flights could serve islands instead of costly airports.
Asked how work is going on an island airport the President has repeatedly promised.
Seconded the nomination of Husnee Mubarik for the Judicial Service Commission.
Supported the report and thanked the committee for its work.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Asked why cars bought with SDFC loans cannot be registered, and why unregistered vehicles keep appearing in Male'.
Proposed Husnee Mubarik for the Judicial Service Commission.
Supported the Independent Institutions Committee's report and praised the committee's work.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Asked where the taxi line service due in July stands, and the policy on parking slots sold earlier and later cancelled.
Asked what security steps follow a reported robbery of airport bank staff at Velana airport.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Asked whether Maldivian companies are protected for airline agent work and why foreigners are working in cargo and airport roles.
Asked whether airlines from China can be charged fees under the free trade agreement, and when RTL starts in Alif Alif atoll.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Raised a point of order asking why the departing member resigned before a replacement is voted on; the chair did not treat it as one.
Supported the committee's report and said theft inside revenue-collecting institutions is weakening the economy.
Described a crude oil transfer case at Thilafushi and the lost cigarette containers, and asked for stronger enforcement of maritime rules.
Said those in charge of institutions should answer to citizens and welcomed the arrests in the cigarette case.

speakers.name: Ahmed Nazim
positions: Presented the Public Safety committee's Customs Service report on smuggled cigarettes and a lost duty of about MVR 47.2 million.
Described the committee's recommendations to Customs and the Home Minister, including staff asset declarations and better monitoring.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Asked how far Kooddoo airport development has got, citing local concern in Thinadhoo, Madaveli and Hoandedhdhoo.

speakers.name: Abdul Hannan Aboobakuru
positions: Asked under what rule some Thilafushi private ports are letting boats unload cargo outside their security fences.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Asked when ferry terminals promised for islands including Fillaadhoo will be built, and why unregistered cars fill Male'.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Asked about progress on the promised parking building, whether the no-parking-sticker promise holds, and who is responsible for unresolved registration problems.

speakers.name: Ahmed Didi
positions: Asked about air-safety and security implications of a foreign military-linked operation at Addu's international airport.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Asked if RTL services will link resorts so staff can commute, and when ministry services move to the Vaguthu platform.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shameez
positions: Asked when Kooddoo airport talks will finish and what action follows loans that the minister said broke the law.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Shujau
positions: Asked whether the MDP has paid the MVR 5.6 million it owed Island Aviation, and when vehicle numbers in Male' rose.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Asked when Addu airport development will finish, why money for air traffic control equipment is delayed, and whether a development plan exists.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Asked why vehicles are held for 48 hours and also fined, and whether apartments in Hulhumale' can get vehicle registration.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Asked why RTL routes in Haa Dhaalu keep being cancelled, and about a cargo ferry and a legal ruling on parking bans.

speakers.name: Ali Moosa
positions: Asked the causes of Island Aviation's reported losses of MVR 41m, 72m and 71m in 2021-2023 and its current condition.

speakers.name: Ahmed Shakir
positions: Asked when RTL starts in Laamu atoll, whether vehicle import has legal limits, and why empty bikes fill roads.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Asked when backup RTL boats reach Haa Dhaalu, when free RTL travel for the sick starts, and whether domestic air fares will change.

speakers.name: Husnee Mubarik
positions: Asked whether Maafaru airport's terminal will be developed and why domestic flights there have been cut.

speakers.name: Hussain Riza Adam
positions: Presented the Independent Institutions Committee's report recommending Mohamed Farusath as president of the Media and Broadcasting Commission.

speakers.name: Ahmed Saleem
positions: As the committee's rapporteur, said the committee worked without obstruction and pledged to push for the theft to be stopped within five years.
Said fixing Customs could raise about MVR 2.5 billion more in revenue and that the Majlis shares responsibility for oversight.

decisions: Minutes of sittings 2025/3/5 to 2025/3/7 were accepted by the Speaker as no amendments were submitted.
Funadhoo member Mohamed Mamdooh replaces Abdul Latheef Mohamed on the Independent Institutions Committee for the PNC.
Husnee Mubarik (Manadhoo) was proposed and seconded for the Judicial Service Commission seat; no other nominations, vote left to voting time.
Debate on the Media and Broadcasting Commission president report was closed after one speaker; decision left to voting time.
The sitting recessed 10:30 to 11:00 while the Customs Service report was being presented.
Hussain Mubarik (Manadhoo) was approved as the Majlis member on the Judicial Service Commission, 58-0.
Mohamed Farusath was approved as president of the Maldives Media and Broadcasting Commission, 49-9.
The Majlis passed the committee's recommendations in item 5 of the Customs Service report, 58-0.
The next Majlis sitting was set for Tuesday 28 October 2025 at 9:00.
